resources.string: "Usually a library it needs (such as libprotobuf) is older than adb itself. Repair updates the package lists and upgrades adb and the libraries it uses."
"adb isn't installed in the terminal yet. This installs the android-tools package (adb, fastboot)."
"Wireless debugging needs Android 11 or newer. On this phone, run \"adb tcpip 5555\" from a computer once, then connect to localhost port 5555 below."
"Open About phone and tap Build number 7 times to unlock Developer options."
"In Developer options, turn on Wireless debugging. Your phone must be on Wi-Fi."
"Ready. Wireless debugging uses a new port each time it turns on; AntiGem finds it for you."
"Notifications are off for AntiGem. The pairing code is entered in a notification, so allow them first."
"Leave the port empty to find it automatically (this phone only). For another device, enter its IP and port."
"When Wireless debugging turns on again, for example after Wi-Fi reconnects, AntiGem finds the new port and connects while it's running."
"Stay in Settings while you do this. Android closes the pairing dialog as soon as you leave it."
"Use this on a split screen, or for another device: enter the port and code shown in the pairing dialog."
"Chat history is off: new messages are not saved. Turn it on in Agent memory & history."
"They are not saved again; new chats are. The chats themselves stay."
"The agents can no longer look it up, and this chat is not saved again. The chat itself stays."
"%1$s · Memories and past chats every agent can use"
"Stored by the bridge next to the agents, so it works in local and server mode."
"A weak model may not follow the memory rules. Turn it off for that agent."
"Memories set to Always are always included in full and do not count."
"Read, edit or remove the chat history the agents can look up"
"Kept while memory is off; agents do not get them"
"No memories yet. Agents save them as you chat, or add one."
"Agents will no longer get it. Chats that already got it keep what they were told."
"Already added: adding it again updates it"
"A different skill named %1$s is installed and will be replaced"
"Reads the screen, taps, swipes, types and takes screenshots. In Accessibility settings, open \"AntiGem Android Automation\" (it may be under Installed apps or Downloaded apps) and turn it on."
"Included with the accessibility service. Apps that block screenshots (banking, DRM video) show up black."
"Android 10 and older can't take screenshots through accessibility; connect ADB below to allow them."
"Adds what accessibility can't do: pressing any key, installing, uninstalling and force-stopping apps, and running adb shell commands."
"The tools install into AntiGem's terminal. Install it in Settings → Terminal & Shell, then come back here."
"The setup script (android-setup.sh) and the adev commands are not part of the app. They are downloaded from the AntiGem plugins repository when you need them."
"Creates a hello-world app in ~/%1$s and builds its debug APK. The first build of each kind downloads Gradle and libraries (several hundred MB) and takes 5–15 minutes; later builds are much faster."

"The Install buttons above open Android's installer. Agents can also install and start apps themselves with adb (and read logcat): install adb below, then connect the terminal's adb to this phone once over Wireless debugging."
"Prints the version of every tool in the container: Java, the SDK platforms, aapt2, adb, Node.js, Flutter, CMake."

"Let agents (and you) create, build and install Android apps right here: Kotlin or Java with Jetpack Compose, Flutter, and React Native. Gradle, the Android SDK and Flutter run in an Ubuntu container (proot-distro) inside the terminal, the same container REA uses."
"Install only what you need: Kotlin / Java first (the others build on it), then Flutter or React Native."
"A fork of the AntiGem plugins repository, for testing changes to the setup."
"Pick what you want to build. Everything it needs is installed for you, one part after another."
"Keep AntiGem open: the screen stays on while this runs. Stopping half way is safe; install the part again to finish it."

"Any agent that can run terminal commands can build apps: Antigravity, Claude Code, OpenCode or Codex. Ask it in chat; the Android Development skill (below) tells it the commands. In the terminal yourself:"

"adev runs a command in the container with Java, the SDK, Gradle, Flutter and Node.js on PATH, in the current folder. adev-new also makes Flutter (flutter) and React Native (rn) projects. Keep projects in the Termux home, not on shared storage."

"A skills-only plugin from the AntiGem plugins repository. It teaches agents to check the setup, install what is missing (asking you first), create projects with adev-new, build with adev, install the APK and fix the usual errors of building on a phone."
"To give an agent the skill, type /plu: in its chat and pick Android Development, or add the plugin in that agent's MCP settings with the Custom Plugin MCP preset."
"Prefer the terminal? These are the same steps as commands."
"Each step can be run again to repair or update it. The skill gives agents these steps too, so you can also ask an agent to set this up."
"Your projects are never deleted. The Ubuntu container itself is removed on the REA page (Delete container), since both use it."
"Create your own / commands for chat. When you send one, the model gets the text it expands to, while the chat keeps showing the short command."
"Use $ARGUMENTS in the expansion to insert whatever you type after the command. A command can also attach a custom AntiGem plugin and one of its skills, like /plu: does."
"e.g. Review $ARGUMENTS for bugs and explain each one"
"The terminal, the IDE backend and the Antigravity language server are ready to run."
"Your phone has a 32-bit processor. The local Linux environment (terminal, IDE backend and agents running on the phone) needs a 64-bit one, so it can't be installed here."
"The shell, core tools and AGY tools are installed."
"AntiGem runs its terminal, IDE and agents on a local Linux system. Choose how to install it."
"This takes a few minutes. You can keep using the app meanwhile."
"Checking the server for the GitHub CLI…"
"Checking the terminal for the GitHub CLI…"
"The GitHub CLI (gh) isn't installed on your server. Install it there, then tap Refresh. For example:"
"gh isn't installed in the terminal yet. This installs the gh package with pkg, so you can sign in to GitHub and use your repositories with git."
"Sign in with your browser: GitHub shows a short code to confirm, then git, the terminal and your agents can use your repositories, private ones too."
"1. Tap the button below: the code is copied and GitHub opens.\n2. Paste the code and approve AntiGem's access.\n3. Come back here; sign-in finishes by itself."
"Classic tokens need the repo and read:org scopes (workflow too, to push GitHub Actions files). Fine-grained tokens work as well."
"Without this, git asks for a password (and fails) on private repositories and on push."
"Not set yet: git won't commit until it knows who you are."
"Your GitHub email is private; %1$s keeps it private and still links commits to you."
"The Android part is added only while the bridge runs on this phone."
"Nothing yet. Examples: \"Reply in Hindi\", \"Never run git push\", \"My projects are in ~/work\"."
"What the agent should know or do"
"New messages will no longer carry it. Chats that already got it keep what they were told."
"Termux-compatible shell, coreutils & toolchain are now active."
"Failed to configure local environment. You can retry below."
"Select how you would like to download and install the Termux rootfs:"
"Downloading and unpacking native Linux toolchain inside your app sandbox."
"Auto-downloads verified AntiGem rootfs (%1$s) with preconfigured tools and environment"
"Pick an existing bootstrap .zip file from device (Offline)"
"Downloads clean official Termux base bootstrap (%1$s) with essential coreutils"
"Logs will appear here once installation begins..."
"This includes your Termux Linux packages, AI configuration, and local SQLite data."
"Safe to clear. Removes temporary logs and cached assets without touching your code or database."
"Performs a complete wipe of all app data, removing Linux packages, accounts, and chats."
"Are you sure you want to wipe all AntiGem data? This will permanently delete all Linux packages, workspaces, accounts, and chats."
"To confirm and permanently wipe all app data and local Linux storage, type the confirmation phrase exactly as shown below:"
"How to lay out a GitHub repo and its %1$s"
"All plugin docs and examples as a ZIP. Copy it to your PC to build plugins there; start with pc-development.md."
"Only add repositories you trust: plugins run code on your device."
"A plugin already uses the folder %1$s. Choose another folder name for this one."
"A plugin already uses this folder name"

"Each REA MCP server lets the agent use the tools of the groups chosen for it (the REA preset in each agent's MCP settings). Open a group to add or remove tools; a tool can be in several groups. Sizes are what a group costs per request on a server that shows its tools directly; on demand, groups cost nothing up front. Tools marked ✎ change things (apps, files, sessions). Changes apply when the server restarts."
"Install REA to see every tool with its description."
"The built-in groups come with REA's setup files. Get them on the REA page (step 1), or create your own group here."
"Only servers that show all tools offer these. New tools from REA updates appear here: add them to a group."
"%1$s tools this REA version doesn't have"
"Install REA (and Refresh tools) to see every tool with its description. Until then only tools already in groups are listed."
"Not in the installed REA's tool list"
"REA installs into AntiGem's terminal. Install it in Settings → Terminal & Shell, then come back here."
"REA's setup scripts (rea-setup.sh, the rea-mcp launcher and the default tool groups) are not part of the app. They are downloaded from the AntiGem plugins repository when you need them."

"REA has over 200 tools. Tool groups decide which tools each REA server lets the agent use; on a server that shows its tools directly, every tool also costs context on each request. Start with the built-in groups and change them any time: add or remove tools, or create your own."
"The default groups come with the setup files."
"Runs rea doctor in the container: it reports which engines REA can use (JADX, apktool, objdump, rizin, adb…). Engines you did not install show as missing, which is fine."

"REA's phone tools (installed apps, pulling APKs, logcat, screenshots, starting apps) use adb. Install adb above, then connect the terminal's adb to this phone once over Wireless debugging. Without it, agents can still read installed apps' APKs: pm path <package> gives the path."

"Let agents take apart Android apps (APK, Flutter, React Native) and native code: decompile classes, read manifests and resources, inspect .so libraries, look at installed apps. REA is an open-source MCP server; AntiGem runs it in an Ubuntu container (proot-distro) inside the terminal."
"Install only the parts you need. Everything for APK analysis takes about 1 GB."
"Pick the parts you need and install them together, or install them one at a time with the button on each. Anything a part needs is added for you."
"REA is not tied to an agent: any agent can use it. Add it where you manage that agent's MCP servers, with the REA preset:"

"Antigravity → MCP Servers → REA
Claude Code → MCP → REA
OpenCode → MCP servers → REA
Codex → MCP servers → REA"
"Install REA and the MCP launcher above first."
"The preset asks how the agent should see REA's tools"
"It also asks which tool groups the agent may use (step 3). You can add REA to several agents, each with its own choice."
"Add a stdio (local command) MCP server with this command and these environment variables. REA_MODE is lazy (on demand) or direct; REA_GROUPS is all or group ids such as core,android."

"A skills-only plugin from the AntiGem plugins repository. It teaches agents how to use REA well (installed apps, split APKs, Flutter, React Native, native code), to check that REA works and tell you what to fix, and how to install REA from the terminal if you prefer that to this page."
"To give an agent the skill, type /plu: in its chat and pick REA, or add the plugin in that agent's MCP settings with the Custom Plugin MCP preset → REA."

"Let agents analyze websites open in AntiGem's browser with REA: page structure, scripts and the APIs they call, libraries and frameworks, network and console errors, accessibility, storage and screenshots. REA only observes; agents open pages and click with the browser MCP."

"REA servers you already added only show the Websites group once it is chosen: open the REA preset in the agent's MCP settings, type the server's name, tick Websites and save. New REA servers include it."

"While this is on, any app on this phone can connect to port %1$s and read or control the pages open in AntiGem's browser, including sites you are signed in to. Turn it on only while an agent analyzes a site and off when you are done. It also turns off when AntiGem closes."
"Prefer the terminal, or setting up Claude Code, OpenCode or Codex? These are the same steps as commands."
"Each step can be run again to repair or update it. The REA skill plugin gives agents these steps too, so you can also ask an agent to install REA for you."
"Remove REA keeps the Ubuntu container (and Java and Node.js in it) for other uses. Deleting the container frees all the space."
"REA is not installed yet. Set it up first, then add the server."
"Server mode is on: agents start MCP servers on the server, where this phone's REA is not installed. REA works when the agent runs on this phone (Settings → Servers & Connectivity)."
"A new REA server (type an existing name to change that one: %1$s)."
"No tool groups yet: download the setup files on the REA page."
"On demand, allowing more groups costs nothing up front. \"Decompiler session\" needs Ghidra, IDA, Hopper or Kuna, which are not installed."
"Directly, each group adds its size (tokens shown on the chip) to every request."
"Removed groups still named here: %1$s. Saving drops them."
"For groups the agent uses all the time: their tools skip the lookup step, but each adds its size to every request. Usually not needed."
"%1$s tools, each one an MCP tool"
"That is a lot: agents get slower and use up their context sooner. Use On demand, or fewer groups."
"Describes the shape of every REA result in the tool list: about %1$s× bigger for tools offered directly. Leave off unless your agent needs it."
"You have unsaved changes in the server settings. Save them with the button at the bottom or discard them."
"Settings saved. Reopening the app connects over SSH, starts the bridge that is already on the server and opens the connections with the new settings."
"Settings saved. Reopening the app restarts the local bridge and daemon so every connection uses the new settings."
"Tap one to load it. Its mode is selected for you; press Save to apply. Update overwrites a profile with what is in the form now (same mode only)."
"Nothing saved yet. Fill in the settings and tap \"Save as profile\"."
"Off by default: anyone using this phone could read them."
"A profile with this name will be replaced."
"\"%1$s\" (%2$s) will be removed from this phone."
"The bridge and the agents run on this phone."
"On your server, reached through the SSH connection: no open ports, no domain, no reverse proxy."
"The bridge and the agents run on your server, reached by a domain or open ports. The app manages them over SSH."
"Picking a profile switches to its mode. Profiles are saved only when you tap Save as profile, and only on this phone."
"Two addresses, e.g. https://bridge.example.com and https://hub.example.com behind nginx/Apache, or http://203.0.113.5:1234 and http://203.0.113.5:1235 straight to the ports."
"Where this phone's bridge and hub listen."
"Test Hub and Test Bridge work once the settings are saved and SSH is connected: the tunnel runs on that connection."
"Used to install, start and stop the bridge, for the terminal and to let the server's agents use this phone's MCP tools."
"not root if you can avoid it"
"The server's SSH key is pinned the first time you connect; a different key later is refused."
"Custom paths used when auto-starting IDE Bridge, AGY Hub, Claude Code and OpenCode"

"• Passed to the bridge on launch (--bin for AGY, --claude-bin for Claude Code, --opencode-bin for OpenCode, --codex-bin for Codex) so auto-start executes the designated binary directly without interactive prompts."
"• Claude Code: the default is AntiGem's launcher, which runs the newest official Claude version through the bundled glibc. Claude updates never replace it."

"• OpenCode: the default is where its installer (and Settings → OpenCode → Install) puts it. The bridge starts it through the bundled glibc, and finds it in the usual folders when this path is wrong."
"• Codex: the default is the Termux package (pkg install codex, also Settings → Codex → Install). The bridge finds it in the usual folders when this path is wrong."
"The secret that protects the bridge. The app starts the server with it. Through the SSH tunnel it is encrypted; it still keeps other users of the server out of the bridge."
"The secret that protects the bridge. The app starts the server with it. Use https:// on the internet: over plain http it is visible on the network."
"12-char token framing localhost requests to prevent unauthorized app access"
"Who handles the termux-* commands (termux-toast, termux-clipboard-get, termux-location, …). One of the two, never both."
"The app isn't installed: termux-* commands say so until you install it or choose Built-in."
"How does AntiGem connect to AGY Hub?"
"AntiGem connects via gRPC-Web to stream live agent steps and tool executions."
"Categorize chat history in drawer under workspace folders matching repository paths"
"The floating pill across the whole app for switching between Chat, IDE, Terminal, Browser and Notes. Choose its layout, items and their order."
"Automatically collapses into a small arrow handle after inactivity"
"Show a dedicated terminal icon on your Android home screen and app drawer"
"Shortcut buttons in the chat's top bar, next to the project name. Turn any on or off (all off is fine) and set their order, left to right."
"Configure local process (Stdio) or remote (SSE) MCP servers. Discovered tools are dynamically available to all models during chat turns."
"Could not retrieve MCP server states. Ensure the Antigravity daemon is running on this device or accessible at the configured Hub URL."
"Add an MCP server to connect SQLite, filesystem, browser automation, or custom local tools to the assistant."
"Are you sure you want to remove \"%1$s\" from global mcp_config.json? The server and its tools will be disconnected."
"Set custom headers like API keys or tokens required by the remote endpoint."
"Runs on your remote server over SSH"
"Direct SSH to Termux sshd without local rootfs"

"Warning: This will perform an Android OS-level data wipe. All installed packages, rootfs, dotfiles, app settings, and history will be completely cleared.\n\nThe app will close and start completely fresh on next launch. Are you sure you want to proceed?"
"To confirm and permanently wipe all app data and local rootfs, type the confirmation phrase exactly as shown below:"
"AntiGem is wiping all local app data, rootfs, and settings.\n\nThe app will automatically close in %1$s seconds. Simply re-open AntiGem to start fresh."
"Stop it before backing up or restoring, so no database is written to while it's being archived."
"The AGY IDE Bridge and Hub server must be offline before running '%1$s'. Would you like to stop the server now?"
"Optionally enter a password to encrypt your backup zip archive. Leave empty for an unencrypted standard zip."
"Saves the Linux system and your home folder to Download/Antigem/backups. Restore it in the installer with \"From a ZIP file\"."
"SSH keys, agent and GitHub logins, shell history. Useful when moving to a new phone or app."
"Select your backup zip archive to restore. Note: your existing ~/.gemini directory will be safely renamed to ~/.gemini.bak first."
"Backup IDE & AGY workspaces or restore from zip"
"No open projects or workspaces detected in the IDE."
"Select a projects backup archive (.zip) to restore projects to their workspace locations."
"Preserves existing code in a backup folder before extracting"
"Overwrites matching files directly inside target directory"
"Protect your local Linux environment, CLI tools, databases, and AI coding workspaces from accidental wipe or uninstall."

"Why enable this? AntiGem hosts a full local Linux environment with your Node/Python packages, Git repos, and active coding projects. An accidental drag-to-uninstall from the home screen wipes all of it permanently.\n\nActivating Android Device Administrator greys out the 'Uninstall' button at the OS level across phone launchers. You can safely disable this anytime if you wish to uninstall."
"💡 Sideloaded App Tip (Android 13+): If your phone shows 'Restricted setting', open App Info > tap the 3 dots in the top right > select 'Allow restricted settings'."

"When enabled (default), tapping 'Clear Data' in Android's phone Settings > App Info opens AntiGem's Safe Space Manager instead of wiping everything instantly with one click. This prevents accidental wipes and allows safe cache-only cleanup.\n\nYou can toggle this off anytime if you prefer the standard raw Android 'Clear Data' button."
"This will remove AntiGem's Device Admin status. The app will become vulnerable to accidental home-screen uninstallation."

"Blocks that need it show as code until you download it again. Compiled TikZ pictures are removed too."
"This custom theme is removed. If it is in use, the default theme takes its place."
"Tap a theme to try it: the app changes behind this panel."
"Install custom AntiGem plugins from ZIP files or from a repository. A plugin can have MCP tools, skills (skills/*.md), or both. Changes apply to the running browser immediately."
"To create a plugin with your model, add Custom AntiGem Plugin Developer in MCP settings. It supplies the SDK, draft editing, installation, updates, tests and worker logs."
"No plugins installed. Choose a ZIP containing manifest.json plus a background worker, a skills/ folder, or both."

In chat, type /plu: to point the model at a plugin or one of its skills. Updating or reloading restarts that plugin's worker; its MCP connection and stored data are kept."
"%1$s (%2$s) is already installed. Update it with this ZIP, or install the ZIP as a separate new plugin?"

"The desktop runs in AntiGem's terminal. Install it in Settings → Terminal & Shell, then come back here."
"AntiGem's own build of Termux:X11, the app that shows the desktop. It runs inside AntiGem, so Android keeps the desktop running at full speed while you use it."
"This Termux:X11 doesn't share AntiGem's UID, so it can't run inside AntiGem. Uninstall it, then install it again."
"The official Termux:X11 is installed. It can't run inside AntiGem, and Android won't install AntiGem's build over it (they are signed differently). Uninstall it first, then install AntiGem's build."
"The terminal part: the termux-x11 command that starts the X server. %1$s goes with %2$s."
"%1$s is installed, but this Termux:X11 needs %2$s. Installing replaces it."
"The X server is running on display :0. Programs started from the terminal with DISPLAY=:0 show up on the desktop."
"Install a browser from tur-repo to browse the web on your desktop."

"Android 12 and newer stop the extra processes of apps once there are more than 32 in total. A desktop starts many, so Android may close it. You can turn this limit off once, over ADB. It stays off until you turn it back on or reset the phone."
"Connect the terminal's adb to this phone first."
"Run Linux desktop apps (a browser, an IDE, office apps) from AntiGem's terminal. Termux:X11 shows the desktop."
"The desktop runs inside AntiGem, so Android won't slow it down or stop it while you use it."
"Don't install termux-x11-nightly from x11-repo: it only works with the official Termux:X11, not AntiGem's build."
